action.rationale: Budget is small (100 < 20·dim = 200) and evaluations are cheap/deterministic, so a light probe (P1–P3) is warranted to read global structure without overspending. This uses ~12% of the budget to guide method choice instead of committing blindly.

With dim=10 and budget=100 (< 30·dim), TuRBO is the most sample‑efficient choice. Probes show strong global structure (P2 fdc_spearman=0.699) while top10_spread_vs_uniform=0.743 suggests multiple basins, so a model-based global method is preferable to local polishing now.

Only 38 evaluations remain (< round_size 50), and TuRBO has not improved for 8 evals after reaching 1775.24 at eval 56. Given deterministic noise and strong global structure (P2 fdc=0.699), a local polish with L-BFGS-B is the fastest way to refine the incumbent now.
